details: Latest US non-farm payroll data for September showed a weaker-than-expected increase of only 29,000 jobs, with the unemployment rate ticking up to 4.2%. This softer labor market report, combined with dovish signals from Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams, has significantly reduced market expectations for an interest rate hike in October, now estimated at around 15%. Markets are now leaning towards a potential December hike if necessary.
title: US Jobs Slowdown Eases Fed Rate Hike Fears

details: While US rate hike expectations have tempered, central banks elsewhere continue to grapple with inflation. The European Central Bank's Philip R. Lane emphasized a data-dependent approach to monetary policy, focusing on medium-term inflation outlook and transmission. Australia's August inflation rose to 4.0%, leading to expectations of further rate hikes from the Reserve Bank of Australia. Japan's Tokyo CPI increased by 2.7% year-on-year in September, prompting signals for gradual tightening from the Bank of Japan, though immediate action is not deemed urgent.
sourceName: European Central Bank (ECB), Seeking Alpha, State Street
title: Global Inflation Concerns Persist Amidst Varied Central Bank Stances

details: Persistent conflict in the Middle East led to increased crude oil prices and refinery margins throughout the third quarter of 2026. Military strikes on energy infrastructure and disruptions in critical shipping lanes, such as the Strait of Hormuz, caused Brent crude futures to surpass $100 per barrel again in September. This geopolitical tension and its impact on energy supply continue to be a significant factor in the global macroeconomic environment.
sourceName: AMRO ASIA, U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
title: Middle East Tensions Drive Up Energy Prices

details: The global macro-financial landscape is marked by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) and ongoing geopolitical tensions. The ASEAN+3 region, for instance, projects robust economic growth of 4.1% for both 2026 and 2027, despite energy shocks, largely driven by the AI investment cycle supporting regional activities. This trend is exemplified by companies like Flex, which announced a $2.0 billion investment in its cloud and power infrastructure segment (Axiom) to capitalize on the increasing demand for AI infrastructure.
title: AI Investment Fuels Optimism Amidst Resilient Global Growth
